sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed this petition being aggrieved by the arbitral award passed by the Special Deputy Commissioner/Arbitrator, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru, in No. LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR /0 5 / 2014-15 dated 27.08.2021 pertaining to Sy. No.73 measuring 615 Sq. feet of Nagasandra village.
.2.

The definite case of the petitioner is that the property of respondent No.1 measuring 615 Sq. feet in Sy. No.73 of Nagasandra village has been acquired under Preliminary Notification issued by the respondent No.2 under Section 3A(1) vide S.O. No.2000 (E) dated 22.11.2006 and Final Notification under Section 3D(1) and (2) vide S.O. No. 1923(E) dated 13.11.2007.

The respondent No.2 has passed the award on 10.04.2008 and awarded a total compensation amount of Rs.2,46,000/-,
which has been received by the respondent No.1 under protest.
Subsequently, on 20.11.2014 the respondent No.1 has filed the A.P. No.5/2022 application for enhancing the compensation at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per Sq. feet.
Accordingly, the application is taken by the respondent No.2 for consideration.

Thereafter, the Arbitrator hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR / 01 / 02 / 03 / 2012-13, 01 / 02/ 04/ 05 / 03 / 2014- 15 dated 27.08.2021.
.4.

Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting aside the following:
:GROUNDS:
The petitioner claims that the impugned is perverse, patently illegal, capricious and goes against the very fundamentals of Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Further, the award passed by the respondent No.3 as on 10.04.2008 but the respondent No.1 approached the respondent No.2 seeking enhancement of compensation as on 20.11.2014 ie..
A.P. No.5/2022 after a lapse of more than 6 years from the date of passing of award by the respondent No.3 and hence claim of the respondent No.1 was barred by time.
The market value determined by the respondent No.2 is contrary to the provisions of NH Act,
Further, the respondent No. 2 ought to have followed Section 3-G(7)(a) of the NH Act.

The respondent No.3 has rightly determined the market value by taking into consideration both the sale statistics as well as the guidance value for the relevant period and there was no scope for interference with the same.
The respondent No.2 has not complied with the provision of Section 28 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act Act while passing the award.

The respondent No. 2 held that as per the aforesaid notification has held that the market value of NA lands situated at Nagasandra village was Rs.700/- per Sq. feet and thereafter added 50% n the guidance value on the ground that the lands are abutting NH and the A.P. No.5/2022 Arbitrator has further added 25% on the guidance value as enhancement and arrived at Rs.1,225/- per Sq. feet i.e., Rs. 700/- + 350/- (50% of Rs. 700/-) + Rs. 175 (25% of Rs. 700) = Rs.
 1,225/- per Sq. feet.
The re-  determination of market value is completely unscientific, irrational and arbitrary.
There are manifest errors in the impugned Arbitral Award and among other grounds, prayed for relief claimed in the petition.

.5. The LRs of respondent No.1and respondent No. 3 though served with the notice,
not chosen to appear before this Court to resist the petition and hence, they were placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through DGP.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-4/CR/05/2014-15 secured from the Arbitrator.

.6. On the basis of above, the point for consideration is that:

Perused the materials on A.P. No.5/2022 record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in Affirmative for the following:
REASONS .8.
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

The respondent No.1 Smt. Bhagyalakshmi Narayan Patel is an owner of the property bearing Sy. No.73 measuring to an extent of 615 Sq.
feet of Nagasandra village and the said property has been acquired for widening of NH-4 under Preliminary Notification dated 22.11.2006 and Final Notification dated 13.11.2007, is an admitted fact.
It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2 has enhanced the compensation from Rs.400/- per Sq. feet to Rs. 1,225/- per Sq. feet.
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.2,46,000/- was disbursed to the respondent No. 1 as compensation.

Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the respondent No. 1 Smt. Bhagyalakshmi Narayan Patel filed an application before the respondent No.2 claiming that she is entitled for compensation at the rate of Rs. 5,000/- per Sq. feet as on 20.11.2014.

On basis of the said application, the respondent No. 2 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ / ARB / NH-4 /
CR / 01 / 02 / 03 / 2012-13, 01 / 02/ 04/ 05 / 03 / 2014-15 dated 27.08.2021.

The respondent No. 2 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs.1,225/- per Sq. feet by adding Rs. 825/- to the compensation decided by the respondent No. 3 i.e.,
Rs.400/- per Sq. feet.
.10.
The said enhancement has been challenged by the petitioner in this petition.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent No. 2 without considering the relevant provisions of NHA Act and also without considering the guidance value or market value of the property as on the date of Preliminary Notification enhanced the compensation by relying on the guidance A.P. No.5/2022 value of the year 2007 published vide notification bearing No. CVC/BUD/5/2006-07 dated 17.04.2007.

The petitioner also claimed that the Preliminary Notification was published as on National Highways Authority Of India vs Bhagyalakshmi Narayan Patel on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55343556/
4 22.11.2006.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, the respondent No.2 ought to have considered the market value of the property of the year 2006 and not of the year 2007.
As the aforesaid notification relied by the Arbitrator came to effect from 19.04.2007 i.e., after lapse of more than 4 months from the date of publication of Preliminary Notification.
Accordingly claimed that the said enhancement cannot be accepted.
It is true that as per the NH Act, the market value of the land as on the date of Preliminary Notification has to be considered.

.11. The petitioner also claimed that whatever the document relied by the respondent No. 2 for enhancing the compensation is not brought to the notice of the petitioner before passing the award/judgment.
Accordingly, claimed that such award is liable to be set aside as per Section 24 of National Highways Authority A.P. No.5/2022 Act.

entities.text: National Highways Authority A.P. No.5/2022 Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In this context, the petitioner relied on the decision reported in (2019) 15 SCC 131 in a case of Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India.

entities.text: Ssangyong Engineering and Construction Company Limited Vs. National Highways Authority of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is true that in the said decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that whatever the document relied by the Arbitrator shall be brought to the notice of the parties, so that the parties can make submission or give a rebuttal evidence about such documents.
However, in the case on hand, such notification is not found in the record received from the Arbitrator.
.12. In the case on hand, the Arbitrator has enhanced compensation to tune of 75%.
There is no reasoning for enhancement of 75% of the compensation amount.

It is simply stated that 75%
compensation has been enhanced as the property has been acquired for the formation of national highway.
It is well settled principle of law that discretion must be used judiciously and not arbitrarily.
Whatever the enhancement has been granted by the Arbitrator, certainly effect the State A.P. No.5/2022 or State Exchequer.
Hence, Arbitrator shall give reasons for enhancement of the compensation.
As already stated above, the Arbitrator / respondent No.3 has not given any explanation for enhancement of 75%.
Hence such enhancement cannot be accepted.

.13. In the case on hand, though the respondent No.1 and 3 served with the notice not chosen to appear before the court to resist the case of the petitioner or to support the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Absolutely there is no material placed before the court to disbelieve the petitioner case or to substantiate the award passed by the respondent No.3.
Hence, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to intervene with the award passed by the Arbitrator and the award is liable to be set aside.
Accordingly, the above point is held in the affirmative.
In the result following.
ORDER Petition is allowed.

Consequently, the award passed by the Arbitrator / respondent No.2 in case No.
LAQ / ARB / NH-4 / CR / 05/ 2014-15 dated 27.08.2021 pertaining to Sy.
No.73 measuring 615 Sq. feet of Nagasandra village is hereby set aside with a liberty to the parties to pursue their remedy in accordance with law.
